messages.subject: Re: ERROR: path[1]="": No such file or directory on shiny 0.6.0.99
parts:
Great! Unfortunately, with that AMI, I think you're best off building R from source in order to update. The alternative would be to rebuild the image using EPEL repo's. But if you've already got an image with R 3, no need!

There are a few threads out there on managing multiple versions of R on a single machine including this one: http://r.789695.n4.nabble.com/Installing-different-versions-of-R-simultaneously-on-Linux-td879536.html

One option is to explicitly install each version of R at a different prefix then set your PATH to ensure that the proper version of R has priority. Or you can just uninstall the old version...

messages.subject: Re: ERROR: path[1]="": No such file or directory on shiny 0.6.0.99
parts:
UPDATE:

I've narrowed down the problem a bit. Here's more details: https://github.com/ramnathv/rCharts/issues/224

Commenting out this portion of code that generates an NVD3 chart, makes the "ERROR: path[1]="": No such file or directory" error go away.
  output$powerPosition <- renderChart2({
    x <- newData()
    x1 <- ddply(x, .(position), summarize, meanPower=mean(power))
    n1 <- nPlot(meanPower ~ position, group = "position", data = x1, type = "multiBarChart")
    #n1$print("chart3")
    n1
    })
